A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SysCaps research. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–B are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original building-energy and wind-farm surrogate experiments, caption-quality measurements, generalization tests and sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original results for both simulators and reports additional encoder comparisons and a randomized building-type control.

M1.justification: The caption-generation pipeline, text/timeseries fusion, encoder alternatives, prediction head and squared-error objective remain unchanged. BERT was already specified and evaluated in v1; its expanded evaluation in v2 does not introduce a new method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same building-energy and wind-farm datasets and tasks. v2 adds testing with randomly incorrect building-type descriptions, extending the input-corruption scenarios beyond the existing synonym and missing-attribute tests.

E2.justification: v2 Table 4 adds a random-building-type baseline to the synonym comparison; v1 Table 3 used attribute removal as its control. The conventional LightGBM and one-hot ResNet, LSTM and SSM comparison methods remain.

E3.justification: v2 extends BERT evaluation to key-value captions with SSM, LSTM and ResNet, beyond v1's reported BERT natural-language SSM comparison. Appendix A also corrects the stated sequence-input dimensions from 103 to 231/871 after concatenation, without establishing that experiments were rerun. Dataset splits and hyperparameter grids remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 expands the encoder comparison and adds the randomized-type robustness control, but removes v1 Figure 5's aggregate error-versus-known-attributes curve. The qualitative missing-information example survives as v2 Figure 3. Appendix B additionally diagnoses a heating-setpoint error in a retained caption; the principal length and sensitivity analyses remain.

E5.justification: v2 Table 1 supplies explicit uncertainty values for the BERT natural-language SSM comparison that v1 discussed only through point estimates. Three-seed averaging and uncertainty reporting already existed elsewhere in v1; no increased run count is stated.

E6.justification: v2 Table 1 substantially expands the main accuracy evidence with BERT key-value results, including stock-annual NRMSE of 0.020, 0.022 and 0.049 for SSM, LSTM and ResNet. The reported SSM/BERT/nl stock-annual value changes from 0.038 to 0.035, and SSM/X from approximately 0.52 to 0.658; the ResNet stock-annual ordering also reverses. Table 4 adds 14 randomized-type results, while the aggregate missing-attribute curve disappears. Wind-farm, caption-quality and caption-length scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, objective and metric equations are mathematically unchanged, and neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs. v2's explanation connecting stock-annual error to normalized bias restates the existing formula.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion strengthen the central accuracy claim from comparable performance or minimal losses with occasional gains to better accuracy than traditional or one-hot methods. Robustness to missing attributes also ceases to be a headline conclusion, although qualitative evidence remains.

C2.justification: v2 Figure 7 reinterprets v1 Figure 1's purportedly successful caption as containing a heating-setpoint error, links such errors to reduced accuracy and recommends domain-expert validation. v2 also removes the analogy between missing-information predictions and low-fidelity surrogates, while retaining the main numerical-tokenization limitations.

D1.justification: v2 documents the one-hot baseline's 128-dimensional embedding and complete concatenated input sizes, discloses held-out validation for the caption classifier, and reports one hour on an A100 for the design-space analysis. These are additional implementation and runtime disclosures; the hyperparameter tables and promised future code/data release remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds Time-LLM, Merrill et al. and Tan et al. on temporal reasoning, and Zhou et al. on sensor-language learning. Related work more explicitly distinguishes simulator regression from forecasting and contrastive pretraining, while retaining the paper's overall research positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract and substantial introductory and related-work passages are rewritten. Caption evaluation becomes a numbered subsection, missing-information discussion is integrated into accuracy evaluation, discussion and conclusion are consolidated, and appendix organization and citation style change.

P2.justification: v2 adds a pipeline overview and a one-hot baseline schematic, replaces the main accuracy bar charts with an expanded numerical table, and removes the aggregate missing-attribute plot. Existing caption examples are relocated and annotated, the synonym table gains a column, and an additional wind-farm example is displayed.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the encoder comparisons easier to verify, strengthens synonym testing with a randomized control, clarifies implementation details and acknowledges a previously unflagged caption error. These improve transparency and support for the framework. The gain is limited by removal of the quantitative missing-attribute plot and broader accuracy claims: the clearest advantages concern stock-annual aggregation, while hourly comparisons remain mixed.
